description: Growth constants for the year-forward DOTAX-shaped calibration targets (calibration/forward_targets.py). Until October 2026 these were literals in build_targets() and _back_cast_cor() with no provenance record; FORECAST_ASSESSMENT_2026-06-11.md P1.6.

low_growth.source: CBO, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2025 to 2035 (January 2025), Table 2-1: nominal wages and salaries +4.0%/yr 2025-2029 national; scaled by the Hawaii wage factor 0.85 used in cbo_aging.DEFAULT_HAWAII_FACTORS and net of ~1pp of filer turnover; held at the 2.5% the model has used since the TY2022 base.

top_differential.unit: per year, nominal, added to low_growth
top_differential.source: IRS SOI Table 1.4 top-1% AGI share, TY2012-2022: +1.8pp/yr relative growth, less the 0.8pp migration haircut (SB3125_CD1_FORECAST.md, top-income premium). forecast_sb3125_vs_fy26base.py overrides this to 0.025 for the MID path.

rate_drift.unit: per year, multiplicative on the per-filer effective rate
rate_drift.applies_to: bracket creep into higher marginal rates within a nominal AGI class
rate_drift.source: DOTAX Table A-8 effective rate on AGI by class, TY2019-2023 editions: within-class effective rates rose 0.3-0.7%/yr relative in the $50K-$200K classes as nominal incomes moved up inside fixed class bounds. Act 46 indexes the standard deduction from TY2024, which lowers the drift; 0.5% is kept as the pre-Act-46 estimate.

population_growth_rate.applies_to: total filer count, applied uniformly across brackets after migration
population_growth_rate.source: DBEDT, Population and Economic Projections for the State of Hawaii to 2050 (DBEDT 2050 Series, April 2024): resident population +0.34%/yr, civilian labor force +0.6%/yr 2025-2035; filers track the labor force. With age-band margins on (calibration/age_targets.py) the total still grows at this rate and the age mix moves with the population projection.

cor_extrapolation_growth.applies_to: COR individual income tax aggregate for years outside the published table (back-cast before the first year, extrapolation after the last)
cor_extrapolation_growth.source: Council on Revenues General Fund forecast, long-run IIT growth after the Act 46 phase-in (FY2030-FY2032 in the March 2026 vintage: +3.7%/yr and +3.3%/yr); 2.5% is the conservative long-run nominal rate the model has carried. Years inside the published table never use it.
